summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with refractory multiple myeloma and MDS with pancytopenia, was admitted for hypercalcemia with a corrected calcium of 11.2 and acute kidney injury, likely due to dehydration and elevated calcium. He was treated with aggressive IV hydration and pamidronate, resulting in normalization of calcium levels and improvement in renal function, with creatinine decreasing from 2.6 to 1.9. His mental status remained stable, and no new infection was found despite a persistent cough; chest X-ray showed no pneumonia. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans to restart lenalidomide outpatient and continue bone-targeted therapy. Medication adjustments included dose reduction of acyclovir and citalopram, and continuation of COPD and pain management regimens.
